inspection_summary.note: Texas HHSC inspections, report investigations and assessments since October 2017, updated daily.

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Grabbing and Pulling: This standard was found to be deficient as part of an investigation. A caregiver was grabbing children as a form of discipline.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Grabbing and Pulling (26 TAC §746.2805(3))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Humiliating, Rejecting, Yelling: This standard was found to be deficient as part of an investigation. A caregiver was yelling at children.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Humiliating, Rejecting, Yelling (26 TAC §746.2805(5))

occurrences.finding: Care Requirements for Toddlers - Individual Attention: This standard was found to be deficient as part of an investigation. A caregiver did not give individualized attention to children by playing with children.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Care Requirements for Toddlers - Individual Attention (26 TAC §746.2501(3))

occurrences.finding: Parental Communication - Situation that Placed a Child at Risk: Based on information obtained through the investigation it was determined that the operation did not communicate effectively when a child was injured on a field trip. The extent of an injury obtained was not relayed in a way that allowed the parent to make an informed decision on whether the child needed medical attention or not.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Parental Communication - Situation that Placed a Child at Risk (26 TAC §746.307(b)(4))

occurrences.finding: Training Requirements for Employees, Caregivers, and Directors - 24 Annual training: At the time of the follow up caregiver files were not updated to have the required trainings.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Training Requirements for Employees, Caregivers, and Directors - 24 Annual training (26 TAC §746.1301(a)(5)(A))

occurrences.finding: Director's Absence -  Caregiver in Charge Has Access to All Records: At the time of the follow up inspection the person in charge did not have access to any updated training records.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Director's Absence -  Caregiver in Charge Has Access to All Records (26 TAC §746.1013(a)(3))

occurrences.finding: Documented Annual Training - Caregivers of Children Under 24 Months Required: At the time of follow up 1 caregiver did not have the required infant care trainings and was in a classroom supervising infants.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Documented Annual Training - Caregivers of Children Under 24 Months Required (26 TAC §746.1309(d))

occurrences.finding: Documented Annual Training - Caregivers of Children Under 24 Months Required: At the time of follow up 1 caregiver did not have the required infant care trainings and was in a classroom supervising infants.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Documented Annual Training - Caregivers of Children Under 24 Months Required (26 TAC §746.1309(d))

occurrences.finding: Orientation-Minimum Standards: At the time of the inspection 2 employees did not have orientation acknowledged as completed in their personnel files.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Orientation-Minimum Standards (26 TAC §746.1303(1))

occurrences.finding: Training Requirements for Employees, Caregivers, and Directors - 24 Annual training: At the time of the follow up 3 of the records reviewed did not have the required 24 hours of annual training.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Training Requirements for Employees, Caregivers, and Directors - 24 Annual training (26 TAC §746.1301(a)(5)(A))

occurrences.finding: Director's Absence -  Caregiver in Charge Has Access to All Records: At the time of the inspection the person in charge did not know the location of CPR/First Aid records for the operation.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Director's Absence -  Caregiver in Charge Has Access to All Records (26 TAC §746.1013(a)(3))

occurrences.finding: Installation and Maintenance of Loose-fill Surfacing - Proper Depth Maintained: At the time of follow up loose fill had not been delivered and all playgrounds had loose fill that did not meet the required depth, and was packed in or deteriorated to dirt.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Installation and Maintenance of Loose-fill Surfacing - Proper Depth Maintained (26 TAC §746.4907(d))

occurrences.finding: Required Records Maintained and Made Available - Personnel and Training Records: Staff Training Records were not immediately available at the time of the visit. Many staff had not printed their certificates from trainings they had completed.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Records Maintained and Made Available - Personnel and Training Records (26 TAC §746.801(3))

occurrences.finding: Installation and Maintenance of Loose-fill Surfacing - Proper Depth Maintained: All playgrounds had loose fill that did not meet the required depth, and was packed in or deteriorated to dirt.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Installation and Maintenance of Loose-fill Surfacing - Proper Depth Maintained (26 TAC §746.4907(d))

occurrences.finding: Safety - Play Materials and Equipment Safe: At the time of the inspection a barrier to contain loose fill had a tear in it that was big enough to stick a pen in with sharp plastic edges. A play structure had rotting wood on a portion that supports a platform. The structure is not in use but still accessible to the children.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Safety - Play Materials and Equipment Safe (26 TAC §746.3701(5))

occurrences.finding: Posting Requirements - List entitled "Current Employees"--sized at least 81/2 X 11 inches, printed legibly, include employee first and last name: A list of current employees was not posted at the operation.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Posting Requirements - List entitled "Current Employees"--sized at least 81/2 X 11 inches, printed legibly, include employee first and last name (26 TAC §746.401(9))

occurrences.finding: Documentation PEDIATRIAC CPR-1st aid original certificate on file at center or copy available if licensing requests: 1 of the 10 files reviewed did not have the first aid/cpr certificate on file for licensing to review.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Documentation PEDIATRIAC CPR-1st aid original certificate on file at center or copy available if licensing requests (26 TAC §746.1329(c)(2))

occurrences.finding: Children's Records - Immunizations: 5 out of the 10 children's records evaluated did not have immunization records available to review.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children's Records - Immunizations (26 TAC §746.603(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Required Personnel Records- Training Hours: 8 out of the 10 personnel file training records were unable to be reviewed by licensing.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Personnel Records - Required Affidavit (Form 2912) (26 TAC §746.901(5))

occurrences.finding: Required Personnel Records - Dates of Employment: 8 out of the 10 personnel records did not have hire dates documented.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Personnel Records - Dates of Employment (26 TAC §746.901(1))

occurrences.finding: Required Admission Information - Date of Admission: 8 out of the 10 children's records reviewed did not have the date of admission documented.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Admission Information - Date of Admission (26 TAC §746.605(3))

occurrences.finding: Required Personnel Records - Required Affidavit: 7 out of the 10 personnel records evaulated did not have employee affidavits on file.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Personnel Records - Required Affidavit (Form 2985) (26 TAC §746.901(4))

occurrences.finding: Maximum Group Size 13 or More Children: The school age exceeded the maximum group size for 2 or more caregivers.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Maximum Group Size 13 or More Children (26 TAC §746.1609)

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: A child was found in room unsupervised.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: Caregiver did not follow procedures during a transition, as a result a child was left in a room unsupervised.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: Nutrition and Food Service - Must not serve identified foods to allergic child: A caregiver served a cupcake to a child who is allergic to eggs.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Nutrition and Food Service - Must not serve identified foods to allergic child (26 TAC §746.3301(i))

occurrences.finding: Installation and Maintenance of Loose-fill Surfacing - Nine Inches if Equipment Greater Than 5 Ft.: It was observed less than 9 inches of loose-fill material around an outdoor play structure that is more than 5 feet tall.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Installation and Maintenance of Loose-fill Surfacing - Nine Inches if Equipment Greater Than 5 Ft. (26 TAC §746.4907(a)(2))

occurrences.finding: Employee Handwashing After Handling or Cleaning Bodily Fluids: A caregiver was observed cleaning a child's nose and did not wash her hands.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Employee Handwashing After Handling or Cleaning Bodily Fluids (26 TAC §746.3415(7))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: A caregiver did not follow the operation procedures while conducting a Name to Face check during a transition.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: A caregiver did not follow the operation procedures while conducting a Name to Face check during a transition as a result a child was left in room unsupervised.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Immunization Records, Exceptions, and Exemptions Current: Three of the children records reviewed, did not have an immunization record on file.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Immunization Records, Exceptions, and Exemptions Current (26 TAC §746.613(b))

occurrences.finding: Required Health Statement - Written, dated within past year, indicates child is physically able to participate in operation's child-care program: Nine of the children files reviewed did not have a health statement on file.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Health Statement - Written, dated within past year, indicates child is physically able to participate in operation's child-care program (26 TAC §746.611(a)(1))

occurrences.finding: Discipline - Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance: A caregiver did not used proper method of discipline, the caregiver hit a child's forehead and send children to the bathroom as timeout.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Discipline - Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance (26 TAC §746.2803(4))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Hitting with Hand or Instrument: A caregiver hit a child's forehead as method of discipline.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Hitting with Hand or Instrument (26 TAC §746.2805(4))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Placing Child in Locked or Dark Room: According to children's statements, a caregiver used to send children to the bathroom as time out.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Restrictive device for time out (26 TAC §746.2805(8))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: A caregiver did not demonstrate good judgment and competency when discipline children under her care, using inappropriate discipline methods.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: Alternate Activity for Non-sleeping Children: An alternative activity was not offered to a non-seeping child during naptime.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Alternate Activity for Non-sleeping Children (26 TAC §746.2907(a))

occurrences.finding: Report Situation Placing Children at Risk: The operation reported to licensing a parent concern about a possible violation of the minimum standard four days after been made aware.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Report Situation Placing Children at Risk (26 TAC §746.305(a)(6))

occurrences.finding: Parental Notification of Less Serious Injuries: This rule was evaluated with regard to an investigation and has been found to be in violation. The center applied Band-Aids to a child, but did not inform the guardian at pick up about the bites and scratches.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Parental Notification of Less Serious Injuries (26 TAC §746.307(c))
